$comment: [X4.8] pgEdge Postgres MCP attach spec. Tier-2 VERIFIED-PUBLISHER (publisher `pgedge` — official pgEdge Postgres MCP server from github.com/pgEdge/pgedge-postgres-mcp; X1.12 evidence; trust.json key is lowercased `pgedge`). Shape === mcp-specs/_template.json (X2.1). Go server shipped as the Docker image ghcr.io/pgedge/postgres-mcp (stdio mode by default); read-only-by-default query surface. CC0-1.0.
title: pgEdge Distributed Postgres
description: Query and analyze PostgreSQL databases — SQL execution, schema discovery, EXPLAIN analysis, and hybrid vector search — via the official pgEdge Postgres MCP server.

env_vars.name: PGEDGE_DB_HOST
env_vars.description: PostgreSQL host to connect to. Provide the connection via these PGEDGE_DB_* vars or a config file.

env_vars.name: PGEDGE_DB_USER
env_vars.description: Database user. Prefer a least-privilege, read-only role.

env_vars.name: PGEDGE_DB_PASSWORD
env_vars.description: Database user password; pass via env, never inline in args (doctrine #6).

env_vars.name: PGEDGE_DB_SSLMODE
env_vars.description: Postgres SSL mode (e.g. require, verify-full, prefer). Use require/verify-full for remote clusters.

env_vars.name: PGEDGE_DB_ALLOW_WRITES
env_vars.description: Set to `true` to allow write queries (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL). Off by default — the server runs read-only transactions.

auth.recipe: point the server at PostgreSQL via the PGEDGE_DB_* variables (host/port/name/user/password) and use a least-privilege read-only role; leave PGEDGE_DB_ALLOW_WRITES unset for read-only access.

sample_tools.name: query_database
sample_tools.summary: Execute a SQL query (runs inside a read-only transaction by default).

sample_tools.name: count_rows
sample_tools.summary: Count rows in a table before querying large datasets.

sample_tools.name: get_schema_info
sample_tools.summary: Discover tables, columns, data types, and relationships.

sample_tools.name: execute_explain
sample_tools.summary: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a SELECT query to analyze performance.

sample_tools.name: similarity_search
sample_tools.summary: Hybrid vector + BM25 + MMR search over pgvector columns.

sample_tools.name: read_resource
sample_tools.summary: Read MCP resources such as pg://system_info.

known_limitations: Connect to PostgreSQL via the PGEDGE_DB_* variables (host/name/user/password) or a config file; without a configured connection the data tools return no results.
Distributed as a Docker image (ghcr.io/pgedge/postgres-mcp) — Docker must be installed and running; there is no npm package.
Read-only by default — query_database runs inside read-only transactions; setting PGEDGE_DB_ALLOW_WRITES=true enables DDL/DML and the server then marks query_database with `destructiveHint`.

Semantic tools (similarity_search, generate_embedding, search_knowledgebase) require extra setup — pgvector columns, an embedding provider, and/or a prebuilt knowledgebase — and are otherwise unavailable.

Destructive-action audit (X2.18): no tools match destructive name patterns (destructive_tools is empty); write capability is gated behind the off-by-default PGEDGE_DB_ALLOW_WRITES and the read-only-transaction guardrail.

client_install.claude_desktop: Add to claude_desktop_config.json mcpServers as `pgedge`: { command: docker, args: [run, -i, --rm, -e, PGEDGE_DB_HOST, -e, PGEDGE_DB_NAME, -e, PGEDGE_DB_USER, -e, PGEDGE_DB_PASSWORD, ghcr.io/pgedge/postgres-mcp], env: { PGEDGE_DB_HOST: "...", PGEDGE_DB_NAME: "...", PGEDGE_DB_USER: "...", PGEDGE_DB_PASSWORD: "..." } }.
client_install.cursor: Settings → MCP → Add: name `pgedge`, command `docker run -i --rm -e PGEDGE_DB_HOST -e PGEDGE_DB_NAME -e PGEDGE_DB_USER -e PGEDGE_DB_PASSWORD ghcr.io/pgedge/postgres-mcp`; set the PGEDGE_DB_* vars in the env.
client_install.vscode: Add to .vscode/mcp.json servers as `pgedge` (VS Code Insider, MCP preview); supply the PGEDGE_DB_* connection vars via inputs.
